summary.headline: R R Kabel Q1 FY27 revenue rose 54% to INR3,168 crore and operating EBITDA nearly doubled to INR285 crore, with FMEG reaching operational breakeven.
summary.overview: R R Kabel delivered its highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT in Q1 FY27, with revenue up about 54% YoY to INR3,168 crore and operating EBITDA margin up to 9% from 7%. Wires & Cables volumes grew 17% YoY, with cables above 25% and wires about 12%, and exports grew in line with domestic despite Middle East disruption that began to normalise in May-June. FMEG revenue grew about 28% to INR288 crore and reached operational breakeven versus a loss of about INR7 crore a year earlier. Management reiterated its FY28 Wires & Cables margin guidance of 10.5% and ~18% volume growth, and cautioned that the quarter is early in the year.

segments.name: Wires & Cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,880 crore (+~57% YoY) and segment profit INR285 crore at 9.9% margin vs 7.6%. Volumes +17% YoY; cables +25%+, wires ~12%; domestic and export grew at similar rates.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Revenue INR288 crore (+~28% YoY), reached operational breakeven vs loss of ~INR7 crore in Q1 FY26 and ~INR9 crore in Q4 FY26. Fans volumes flat YoY but revenue up on realisation and premium mix; ~25% of FMEG revenue from premium products.

guidance_outlook: Wires & Cables EBITDA/segment margin guidance of 10.5% by FY28 maintained; management endeavours to be in double digits for FY27 but says it is early in the year.
Margin target of +100 bps YoY reiterated for the year.
Volume growth of ~18% YoY expected for FY27, consistent with long-term guidance given at start of FY26.
FMEG: breakeven on a yearly basis targeted for FY27 (Q2 typically weaker, so quarterly breakeven not assured); ~20% top-line growth targeted and sustained profitability over 2-3 years.
Pricing: if current prices hold, Q2 pricing could reflect ~30% LME-linked increase; management later estimated net ~40% metal price impact translating to ~25% overall product pricing.
H2 expected to be stronger than H1, consistent with historical pattern.
capex_capacity: Project RRise capex plan of ~INR1,200 crore over FY26-FY28; ~INR300 crore spent in FY26 and ~INR600-650 crore planned in FY27; ~80% towards cables.
New wire capacity to be added at Silvassa in the current quarter (Q2 FY27).
Cable capacity additions planned at Waghodia during FY27.
Management plans to increase HV cable presence (currently mainly LV).
demand_pricing: Industry Wires & Cables growth estimated at 10-12% in Q1 by management (rough view).
Management says the Middle East disruption was offset by other export markets; shipments normalised in May-June, though supply chain issues persist.
Europe and Middle East are the largest export contributors; US seen as a new opportunity pending tariff clarity, with a few approvals in hand.
Data centre business is at announcement stage with a few orders received; share in revenue described as very small.
North and West contribute ~65% of domestic revenue; East still small, South improving.
Retail touch points >150,000; ~20,000-25,000 retail points added last year, while dealer count is expected to decline as the company consolidates distribution.
Management attributes ~2-3% annual shift from unorganised to organised market.
Management said competitive pricing pressure not seen specifically in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Where are cable market share gains coming from, and how far can cable margins improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is mainly through distribution channel, with B2B/project focus building; management maintained 10.5% FY28 margin guidance, noting it is early in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 quarter-end channel stocking or destocking impacting volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the last part of the quarter saw a negative impact on volume growth from destocking, but expects business-as-usual over the longer term.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FMEG breakeven delayed versus earlier target of Q4 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Sharp raw material price increases prevented breakeven in Q4 FY26; Q1 FY27 achieved it, with yearly breakeven targeted for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the other income jump a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not call it a normal run rate; a weaker dollar boosted gains for this export-heavy company and is part of business.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 9.9% Wires & Cables margin driven by inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed there was no inventory gain or loss; improvement is organic from scale, absorption and mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the implied pricing growth from metal prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management indicated ~40% net metal price impact translating to ~25% overall product pricing, after earlier ~30% LME estimate for Q2 versus prior-year Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why do domestic and export margins differ across wires and cables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wires are a consumer brand product in India earning premium margins, while export cables need precision and approvals; domestic cable margin is 6-7% and expected to reach 10-11% at scale.

risks_watch: Metal price and FX volatility; pricing lags and inventory effects on margins.
Destocking at quarter-end could weigh on Q2 volumes.
FMEG quarterly breakeven unlikely in seasonally weaker Q2; sustained profitability still to be proven.
Middle East supply chain normalisation remains incomplete; US tariff outcomes unclear.
Other income rise, partly FX-driven, may not recur and flatters PAT.
Wires utilisation of 65-70% and dealer count consolidation to monitor.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and reiterates long-term targets, but cautious on full-year phasing, noting it is early in the year and that Q2 FMEG may not break even. Some answers on pricing and inventory were vague or required follow-up clarification.
key_quotes: During the quarter, we delivered our highest ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and profit after tax.
Overall, Wires & Cable volumes grew by 17% year-on-year with similar growth seen both in domestic and export markets.

So overall, in export wire margins will be less, but in domestic wires, we have higher margins, while in export cables, margins are already good, but in domestic cable also, our margins are improving in current phase.

But at the same time, since Q2 is a little bit lower in FMEG side, this quarter may not be possible, but we are -- we'll try to achieve it, but on a yearly basis, we are quite sure to achieve breakeven in this year.
